newsitem.title: USA: BPA cuts Thurs peak firm power by $1/MWh.
newsitem.headline: BPA cuts Thurs peak firm power by $1/MWh.

text.p: The Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) cut prices for Thursday peak firm power by $1.00 a megawatt hour (MWh) and increased sales volume to 300 MW from 200 MW the previous day, BPA said Wednesday.
BPA offered Thursday peak firm power at $17.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) for Northwest deliveries and $19.00 for California-Oregon border (COB) sales.
BPA's Thursday price for firm power during light load hours was unchanged at $9.00 for both the Northwest and COB.
BPA also left Thursday prices for non-firm power during hours ending 0100-0500 and 2400 PDT at $9.00 per MWh. Non-firm power during hours ending 0600 and 2300 PDT was unchanged at $10.00.

The agency also offered power for the Friday Independence Day holiday at the same prices for light-load hours. An unlimited volume of peak firm power was offered for Friday at $10.00 for Northwest deliveries and $12.00 for COB.
Non-firm power during peak hours on Friday was offered at $11.00 a MWh for Northwest sales and $13.00 for COB.
